title: Benchmark dataset for motion-corrupted patch ECG and simultaneous accelerometry in free-living adults

record.title: Benchmark dataset for motion-corrupted patch ECG and simultaneous accelerometry in free-living adults
record.abstract: High-quality annotated datasets pairing ambulatory ECG recordings with synchronised inertial data from the same wearable patch remain scarce, hampering reproducible research on motion-artifact suppression and context-aware cardiac monitoring. This paper describes the NovaSAD-PatchECG dataset: 128 recordings of 48 hours each, collected from 64 healthy volunteers and 64 patients with known arrhythmia history. Each recording includes single-lead ECG sampled at 500 Hz, three-axis accelerometer data at 100 Hz, and ground-truth rhythm annotations produced by two independent cardiologists with inter-annotator agreement reported via Cohen's kappa. Participants performed a standardized protocol encompassing controlled laboratory activities and unrestricted daily life. The dataset captures a diverse range of motion intensities, electrode contact qualities, and arrhythmia types. Baseline performance figures for three published AF detectors are reported to facilitate fair future comparisons. The dataset is released under an open-access licence and accompanied by Python-based loading utilities. We anticipate that this resource will accelerate development and fair benchmarking of wearable cardiac monitoring algorithms, particularly those addressing false-alarm reduction and real-time on-device inference.
